name: HashiCorp Vault
description: Protects against destructive Vault CLI operations like deleting secrets, \ disabling auth/secret engines, revoking leases/tokens, and deleting policies.

destructive_patterns.name: vault-secrets-disable
destructive_patterns.description: vault secrets disable disables a secrets engine, causing data loss.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Disabling a secrets engine permanently deletes ALL secrets stored in that \ engine. Dynamic credentials are revoked immediately. Applications using \ secrets from this engine will fail authentication. This cannot be undone.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault secrets list: Review enabled engines first \ - Export secrets before disabling \ - Rotate applications to new secrets engine first

destructive_patterns.name: vault-kv-destroy
destructive_patterns.description: vault kv destroy permanently deletes secret versions.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Destroy permanently erases secret data including all specified versions. \ Unlike delete (which is soft-delete in KV v2), destroy is irreversible. \ The data cannot be recovered even by Vault administrators.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault kv delete: Soft-delete with undelete option \ - vault kv get: Verify the secret versions first \ - Export secret data before destruction

destructive_patterns.name: vault-kv-metadata-delete
destructive_patterns.description: vault kv metadata delete removes all versions and metadata for a secret.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting metadata removes ALL versions of a secret and its metadata \ permanently. This is more destructive than destroy as it removes the \ entire secret history. The secret path becomes available for reuse.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault kv metadata get: Review secret metadata first \ - vault kv destroy: Delete specific versions only \ - Export all secret versions before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: vault-kv-delete
destructive_patterns.description: vault kv delete removes the latest secret version.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
In KV v2, delete performs a soft-delete of the latest version. The data \ can be recovered with undelete until the delete_version_after policy \ expires. In KV v1, delete is permanent and immediate.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault kv get: Verify the secret before deleting \ - vault kv undelete: Recover if mistakenly deleted (v2) \ - Set appropriate delete_version_after policies

destructive_patterns.name: vault-delete
destructive_patterns.description: vault delete removes secrets at a path.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
The generic delete command removes data at the specified path. The \ behavior depends on the secrets engine. For most engines, this is \ a permanent deletion of the secret data.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault read: Verify the path contents first \ - Use engine-specific commands for safer operations \ - Back up data before deletion

destructive_patterns.name: vault-policy-delete
destructive_patterns.description: vault policy delete removes access policies.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Deleting a policy immediately affects all tokens with that policy. Users \ and applications may lose access to secrets they need. Orphaned tokens \ retain their policy name but lose the permissions.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault policy read: Review policy before deletion \ - vault token lookup: Check affected tokens \ - Create replacement policy before deleting

destructive_patterns.name: vault-auth-disable
destructive_patterns.description: vault auth disable disables an auth method.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Disabling an auth method revokes ALL tokens issued by that method and \ removes all configuration. Users authenticating via this method will \ immediately lose access. This includes all associated roles and policies.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault auth list: Review auth methods first \ - Migrate users to another auth method \ - Export auth configuration before disabling

destructive_patterns.name: vault-token-revoke
destructive_patterns.description: vault token revoke invalidates tokens and can disrupt access.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Revoking a token immediately invalidates it and all child tokens. \ Applications using this token will fail authentication on next request. \ With -prefix, all tokens under a prefix tree are revoked.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault token lookup: Verify the token before revoking \ - Use token TTLs for automatic expiration \ - Coordinate token rotation before revocation

destructive_patterns.name: vault-lease-revoke
destructive_patterns.description: vault lease revoke invalidates leases and can disrupt access.
destructive_patterns.explanation:
Revoking a lease immediately invalidates dynamic credentials (database \ passwords, AWS keys, etc.). Applications using these credentials will \ fail. With -prefix, all leases under a path are revoked.

\ Safer alternatives: \ - vault lease lookup: Review lease details first \ - Use shorter TTLs for automatic rotation \ - Coordinate credential rotation before revocation
